dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt system (JMA standard receipt software), Japanese medical billing, GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux/Unix environment evidenced by /var/tmp/ file paths and COPY .INC copybooks

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance billing system (ORCA) - inpatient medical treatment batch registration/processing (Nyuin Shinryo Koi Ikkatsu Toroku)
purpose.summary: This program is part of the JMA ORCA standard medical receipt software system. It performs batch registration and processing of inpatient medical treatment actions (Nyuin Shinryo Koi Ikkatsu), reading work files and parameter files, validating data, and producing error and confirmation lists. It handles patient master, insurance combination, treatment activity records, and outputs error reports with counts.

notable_features: 58 COPY statements referencing JMA ORCA-specific copybooks (.INC files)
40 CALL statements indicating heavy use of subprogram architecture
Large OCCURS tables (up to 600 entries) for sort work areas
Japanese text in comments and data literals (latin-1 encoded Shift-JIS/EUC-JP)
File paths using /var/tmp/ indicating Linux/Unix runtime
REPLACING clause in COPY for record prefix substitution
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
Sequential file I/O with FILE STATUS
Error list and confirmation list output structures
verdict.notes: Source is truncated at 16000 chars out of 111149 bytes (2635 lines total). Japanese text in comments and literals is encoded as latin-1 decoded bytes, likely originally EUC-JP or Shift-JIS. The program is clearly part of the well-known JMA ORCA open-source Japanese medical receipt system, targeting GnuCOBOL on Linux.
